title: attribution alternatives that actually work
claim: Multi-touch attribution is a bookkeeping convention with no control group; the three-question stack replaces it.
hook: Your attribution dashboard is lying to you.

evidence.detail: Forrester found that 64% of B2B marketing leaders do not trust their measurement, and only 6% are advanced insight-driven businesses.

slides.headline: Your attribution dashboard is lying to you.
Attribution assigns credit by correlation, not cause.
slides.body: It rewards the last thing a buyer touched before doing what they were already going to do.

slides.headline: Stop asking one model to answer three questions.
slides.body: Allocation, causality, and brand memory require three separate measurement layers.

slides.headline: Mix modelling answers where money goes over a year.
slides.body: Tools like Meta Robyn and Google Meridian are open-source and free. The cost is data cleanliness.

slides.headline: Incrementality testing proves if spend caused sales.
slides.body: A geographic holdout gives you the one number that survives an argument with finance.

slides.headline: Share of search tracks long-term brand memory.
slides.body: It is the cheapest signal available for whether your brand is getting easier to sell.

slides.headline: Finance teams work in ranges. Marketing should too.
slides.body: Replace false decimal precision with an experimental range and a control region.

slides.headline: Measurement requires a control group, not a dashboard.

caption:
Your attribution dashboard is lying to you.

Evaluating marketing attribution alternatives proves why.

Most teams run dashboards they privately do not believe. Forrester found that 64% of B2B marketing leaders distrust their own measurement.

The fix is separating allocation, causality, and memory into distinct layers.

Send this to whoever is defending the quarterly marketing report to the board this week.
